title: Bahadur Shah Hears of Banda’s Rise

blocks.text: Petitioners at court portray Banda as the Guru’s Sikh who has already overthrown officials, ravaged key towns, and become a threat to Mughal-held settlements, forcing Bahadur Shah to confront his rising reputation.

The emperor hears repeated accounts that weapons do not strike Banda properly, that he moves with uncanny lightness, and that people around him read these things as signs of karamat rather than ordinary warfare.
Bahadur Shah is therefore introduced here not as a bold conqueror but as a ruler already anxious before Banda’s name and the aura around him.
